objects.why: Journaling, writing down thoughts on paper to externalize and filter mental chatter.
The cash value of ideas in pragmatism: what practical difference does a belief make.
Moments of clear, intentional insight vs unvetted mental chatter.
Digital distractions, unread emails, and modern noise triggering involuntary thoughts.
Focusing on actionable problems and directing attention with intention.
Focusing on direct productive action rather than narrating one's own life.
Interrogating and cross-examining recurring anxious thoughts.
Balancing mental energy and weighing decisions pragmatically.

spine.claim: Most human thinking is automatic, involuntary chatter that drains mental energy without solving problems.
Pragmatism offers a filter: evaluate every thought by its tangible, practical cash value in real life.
Externalizing thoughts onto paper breaks cognitive spirals and turns vague anxiety into solvable decisions.
Action cures overthinking; treating life as a laboratory eliminates the paralyzing fear of imperfect outcomes.
Mental clarity is an active discipline of choosing which thoughts to entertain and discarding the rest.
